newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro adopts 1997 draft budget - Tanjug.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro adopts 1997 draft budget - Tanjug.

text.p: The Montenegrin government has adopted its 1997 draft budget at a little under two billion dinars, Tanjug news agency reported Thursday.
"The draft budget stands at 1.99 billion dinars ($390 million)," the Montenegrin information ministry was quoted by Tanjug as saying.
It said the budget would be used to finance (Montenegrin) state administration and judiciary, science and education, sports, culture, social security, public works and public information.
The 1997 budget spending policy is based on financing from real sources and maintaining balanced budget.
In November the government of Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, adopted a 1997 draft budget of 9.238 billion dinars. The federal budget covers federal administration and defence costs
On Wednesday Serbia also adopted its draft budget at 14.060 billion dinars.
Yugoslavia's GDP is slated to rise 13 percent in 1997 to 103 billion dinars, according to official forecasts. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4305
